messages:
emma: Heads-up: noticed a weird parity bug after bumping OkHttp -> 4.11 in the Android SDK. App shows occasional requests hitting the server with no Authorization header after a keepalive/connection-eviction followed by an immediate retry. repro in samples/keepalive-evict.zip
lucas: hmm, do you have logs? is it only with streaming bodies or all requests?
emma: mostly POSTs with a small JSON body during onboarding. Steps: run sample with low keepalive (5s), wait for eviction, then trigger request. Logs:
```
I/OkHttp: Connection released to pool
I/OkHttp: Connection evicted by keepAlive
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/onboard (id=0xabc)
I/OkHttp: <-- 307 Follow-Up (new connection)
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/onboard (id=0xabc-clone)  // server sees this with no Authorization header
E/Server: missing auth header -> 401
```
noah: interesting. Our auth logic runs as an EventListener that injects header when the call is started. If OkHttp creates a follow-up on a different internal path, EventListener callbacks might not fire for the cloned follow-up the same way. Application interceptors are safer for header injection.
lucas: right — EventListener is not a request-transform hook. It’s for observability. If we mutate outgoing request state there we rely on side effects. We should move Authorization insertion into an application interceptor so every attempt gets the header deterministically.
emma: ah that explains the missing header. I accidentally put the header add into the auth-observer since I wanted telemetry about token age at call time. Bad idea.
noah: also note that our suspend CallAdapter does a `call.clone()` and then applies an updated header builder returned from auth helper. But if the auth helper mutated a shared Request.Builder instance earlier (the bad pattern), clones won't pick that up.
lucas: propose fixes: (1) move auth header insertion into a lightweight ApplicationInterceptor that always runs before network interceptors, (2) avoid relying on EventListener for request mutation, (3) in adapter, ensure clone() is followed by a fresh `request.newBuilder().header("Authorization", token)` before enqueue.
emma: patch idea:
```
class AuthInterceptor: Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    val token = tokenProvider.getTokenBlocking() // fast path
    val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
      .build()
    return chain.proceed(req)
  }
}
```
lucas: + add a defensive test in samples that toggles connection keepalive and asserts server saw Authorization on every attempt. We'll add an emulator matrix job for Pixel-7a:13 with low keepalive and flaky network.
noah: Note: this also touches call retry ordering. If server returns 401 we should use Authenticator interface rather than retrying from adapter to avoid duplicate refreshes. Keep adapter simple.
emma: I'll open WIP PR with AuthInterceptor + adapter change + sample test. tagging @ci-bot to run keepalive-eviction-smoke.
ci-bot: Job queued: keepalive-eviction-smoke #303 (matrix: pixel-7a:13). ETA ~9m :gear:
lucas: once merged, update devex/samples doc about "Where to mutate requests: Interceptor vs EventListener" and add a short note to CHANGELOG under java/kotlin sdk: "fix: ensure Authorization header on follow-up requests after connection eviction".
emma: thanks — adding unit tests and the sample harness. Will backport to 0.13.x if QA reproduces on older clients.
